items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: We finally got Noah Dutrae and Johnny, you see, myself... organized our regular group. We had Noah Dutrae, we had Jimmy Pilar, Johnny Dodge...

ctx.x: Oh yeah? Garland's New Orleans Jazz Band. Uh-huh. Jazz band, yeah.

Then, uh, Johnny Dodds come in town. We got a hold of Johnny Dodds. Nora Dutre was in the neighborhood. He used to come into Chicago and he'd come sit in with us. So, uh, Boyd H. Williams opened up the, uh, the, opened up this club on 34th Street, uh, Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland…
Was it hard to find a piano player at the time?

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] How about Dodds? >> [INTERVIEWEE] Johnny Dodds? ... [INTERVIEWER] Is that later, Baby Dodds. He came up. >> [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. And his brother Johnny. ... >> [INTERVIEWEE] On the piano. Johnny Dodds on the clarinet.

ctx.x: My brother had a bass. He bought a bass from Sam Nicholson. And he used to tell me to never touch this bass. I'd say, 'Don't worry, Johnny. I ain't going to mess with the bass.' He said, 'You'd better not.' I said, okay, brother. So one day I looked up at that bass, you know, and I said, 'I believe I can play this bass.' I went and got the bass, and I started to messing around with it, and my grandmother said to me, 'Put that bass down. You know your brother don't want you to play that bass.' I said, 'Please let…

just think I can play it." He said, "I'm going to see." So he went and got the guitar. He got the guitar, and the first thing, he started to make a few chords. He played a C, you know. So he says to me, "Let me see what you can do. You say you can play the bass." So I grabbed the bass, and the first thing I hit was F.
